ui.panel.intro:
Click a country or region on the map (or search above) to see who it trades with and how that changed over time.

  • Drag the time slider or press ▶ to animate. Switch to Monthly for detail, or open a Story for a guided replay.
  • “Treat as one” merges countries into a bloc, e.g. the EU.
  • Δ modes color by growth instead of size.

ui.about.title: About the data
ui.about.trade.title: Trade values
ui.about.trade.intro: Bilateral merchandise (goods) trade from the {imf}, formerly the {formerly}. Coverage: {coverage}, in current US dollars (not adjusted for inflation or seasonality). Services trade is not included.
ui.about.trade.reported: Each country's figures are as reported by that country (the selected focus). Because exports are valued FOB and imports CIF, and because of timing, re-exports and confidentiality, A's reported exports to B rarely equal B's reported imports from A. The IMF fills gaps for non-reporting economies with estimates derived from partner data. Taiwan, China is not published as a reporter by the IMF, so its figures here are built from partners' reports ("mirror" data). Recent periods are shown only once most countries have reported them, and may still be revised.
ui.about.trade.monthly: Monthly values are not seasonally adjusted. The Δ 1 yr mode compares each month with the same month a year earlier, which removes most of the seasonal pattern.
ui.about.products.title: Trade by product
ui.about.products.text: When a product is selected, figures come from {baci}: annual, {span}. BACI reconciles what exporters and importers report into one value per flow, valued FOB, so its totals differ somewhat from the IMF figures shown for all goods. Products are groups of HS 1992 codes:
ui.about.products.other: codes not in any other sector
ui.about.ind.title: Economic indicators and correlations
ui.about.ind.source: GDP, population, inflation, unemployment, foreign direct investment, the current account and trade as a share of GDP come from the {wb} (annual). GDP per capita is GDP divided by population; real GDP growth is the change in GDP at constant prices. The World Bank does not cover Taiwan, China.
ui.about.ind.groups: For merged groups, GDP, population, FDI and the current account are summed over the members of each year, and only shown when members with data hold at least 95% of the group's population. Group growth compares the same members in both years. Unlike group trade, these sums include flows between members (for example, investment from one EU country into another counts as EU FDI inflow). Inflation, unemployment and trade % of GDP are not computed for groups.
ui.about.ind.compare: Compare plots one dot per economy for the selected year. Pearson's r is computed on the plotted scale (log10 for log axes, which suits values spanning many orders of magnitude); Spearman's ρ uses ranks, so it does not depend on the scale and is less sensitive to outliers. The dashed line is a least-squares fit on the plotted scale. A country panel's "Do exports move with GDP?" chart correlates year-on-year % changes rather than levels, because any two series that grow over time look correlated. Correlation does not show cause and effect.
ui.about.groups.title: Groupings
ui.about.groups.text: When a grouping is “treated as one”, its members' flows are summed and trade between members is excluded, so the group is shown trading only with the outside world. Membership is applied as of each year: for example, the UK is part of the EU through 2020 and Croatia from 2013. Groups are defined from {m49} or explicit member lists:
ui.about.change.title: Change modes
ui.about.change.text: Δ 1/5/10 yr colors each partner by the ratio between the selected period and the same period that many years earlier (shown as % change, log scale from −75% to +300%). For the balance metric, change is the difference in US dollars.
ui.about.stories.title: Stories
ui.about.stories.text: Stories are guided replays of past events. Figures quoted in a story are computed from the data on this site; other facts link to their sources in the story card.
ui.about.map.title: Map
ui.about.map.text: Boundaries from Natural Earth (1:50m, public domain) via the world-atlas package. Their use does not imply any position on the legal status of any territory. Areas with no matching trade data are grey.
